subject: Computer Science
notes: Single tier. Paper 1 covers computer systems (topics 1–6); Paper 2 covers algorithms, programming and logic (topics 7–10). Content matches the A*–G version (0478). Programming answers should use Cambridge-style pseudocode unless a language is requested; Python, Visual Basic and Java are the accepted high-level languages.

topics.title: Data representation
subtopics: Representing sound and images (sample rate, resolution, colour depth)
File size calculations and units (KiB, MiB …)

topics.title: Data transmission
subtopics: Serial and parallel; simplex, half-duplex and full-duplex
Error detection: parity, checksums, echo checks, check digits, ARQ

topics.title: Hardware
subtopics: CPU and von Neumann architecture; registers and buses
Primary and secondary storage; virtual memory; cloud storage
Network hardware: NIC, MAC and IP addresses, routers

topics.title: The internet and its uses
subtopics: Cyber security threats (malware, phishing, pharming, DDoS, brute force, social engineering…)
Security solutions (firewalls, proxies, SSL/TLS, two-step verification, anti-malware…)

topics.title: Automated and emerging technologies
subtopics: Automated systems: sensors, microprocessors and actuators
Artificial intelligence and machine learning; expert systems

topics.title: Algorithm design and problem-solving
subtopics: Standard methods: linear search, bubble sort, totalling, counting, max/min/average
Test data: normal, abnormal, extreme and boundary
Finding and correcting errors in algorithms

topics.title: Programming
subtopics: Sequence, selection (IF, CASE) and iteration (FOR, WHILE, REPEAT)
Procedures, functions, parameters; local and global variables

topics.title: Databases
subtopics: Single-table databases: fields, records, data types
SQL: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, ORDER BY, SUM, COUNT

topics.title: Boolean logic
subtopics: Logic gates: NOT, AND, OR, NAND, NOR, XOR
Logic circuits from problem statements and expressions
